sara_support: FYI — Acme reported a large unexpected credits burn overnight (~48k tokens). They say their scheduled embedding job ran twice.
kevin_cs: Ticket #3489. Customer runs a nightly batch to /v1/embeddings and then /v1/rerank. They saw identical payloads at 00:01 and 00:02 UTC.
jia_eng: Can you paste the request IDs or any invocation IDs from their logs? could be a retry cycle or callback ack issue.
sara_support: They provided two request IDs: req_abc123 and req_def124. Both show 200 responses in our access logs with matching payloads.
marcus_oncall: Looking at the internal trace for those req ids — enqueue -> worker start -> worker complete -> callback ack timed out -> scheduler requeued the job. Worker didn't check a dedupe key so second run re-sent the same batch to embeddings and rerank.
sara_support: Customer code uses our python SDK in a simple cron: runs embeddings for 10k texts and posts results. No idempotency header set, and their cron wrapper retries on any non-2xx. So if callback latency > timeout they requeue.
kevin_cs: They also called rerank on the same items; rerank token counts doubled as well. Customer is asking for credits refund and a mitigation plan.
jia_eng: This is expected behavior today — embeddings & rerank are stateless and billed per call. We rely on callers to supply Idempotency-Key for dedupe. We should document this more clearly for scheduled jobs and consider defensive dedupe in the batch worker.
sara_support: Proposed immediate mitigation for customer: pause the cron for tonight, restart with idempotency in headers (sha256 of payload) and reduce retry_on_failure in their wrapper. Also offered to hold credits while we investigate.
kevin_cs: I'll put the account on temporary credit hold and escalate the billing review.
marcus_oncall: I'll file a runtime bug to add a request-hash dedupe step in the batch worker and log a request_hash for easier triage. ETA for a canary: tomorrow morning.
sara_support: Sending a short repro checklist to customer now. Repro steps we gave them: 1) schedule a job that POSTs identical payload twice within 2 minutes; 2) simulate callback ack timeout by delaying callback handler; 3) observe two 200 responses in access logs and two billed jobs.
sara_support: Example guidance we pasted (python):
```python
import hashlib, json, requests
payload = json.dumps(batch)
key = hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY", "Idempotency-Key": key}
requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings", data=payload, headers=headers, timeout=60)
```
billing-bot: Billing case BC-2026-118 opened and flagged for credits refund assessment.
deploy-bot: Canary patch queued: PR #4123 — add request-hash dedupe in batch worker (will also emit request_hash header).
marcus_oncall: After patch we should also add a KB doc for scheduled jobs and an SDK snippet recommending Idempotency-Key.
kevin_cs: Thanks — I'll update the customer with the mitigation steps and the temporary credit hold. :thumbsup:
sara_support: Marking thread resolved for support side once customer confirms paused cron and idempotency applied.
